changelog:
0.37.0

  • Active Redirects are sorted alphabetically instead of newest-first, so a store is where you expect it rather than wherever it happened to be created.
  • Search box on the redirect list — matches the name, the /stores/ path and the destination URL, so you can find one by Chipply link as well as by name.
  • The count beside the heading follows the search, showing how many matched.

0.36.0

  • Vendors is a top-level tab now rather than buried under Other.
  • Tabs across the top read Schedule, Quote, Online Stores, Redirect, Vendors — Quote moved ahead of Online Stores.
  • Other still holds Contacts, Exchanges, OMG Scanner and Chipply Scanner.

0.35.1

  • Removes the AWS account from the vendor list. It was imported in 0.35.0 and should not have been — that single login controls the server, the website and every @boomerts.com mailbox, and every portal user can read this list. Updating deletes the entry, including on sites where 0.35.0 already imported it.

0.35.0

  • Eleven more accounts imported from the part of the sheet below the first paste: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Spotify, SocialBee, AWS, the Synology server, WordPress, the Roland cutter laptop and the production Windows login.
  • Imports are additive now and matched on name, so later batches can be added without touching anything already edited in the portal.
  • WordPress went in without a password because none was recorded on the sheet — add it with EDIT on that row.

0.34.0

  • Fixed a way vendor passwords could have quietly become unreadable. The key that unlocks them is written to a file in the uploads folder. If that folder was not writable the write failed silently and a brand new key was generated on every page load — meaning every stored password would decrypt to nothing, and nobody would find out until they pressed SHOW.
  • The key now falls back to the database if the file cannot be written, so it survives either way, and an admin notice explains the trade-off and how to restore the stronger setup.

0.33.0

  • Notes are visible on the vendor list without clicking. A Notes column now shows the first line inline — rep names, RA instructions, the warnings that matter — so most vendors read at a glance.
  • The expand caret only appears when something is actually hidden: a second line of notes, a long one, an address or a fax. Rows with nothing more to show no longer offer a click that reveals nothing.
  • Hovering a truncated note shows the whole thing as a tooltip; expanding the row wraps it in full.

0.32.0

  • Two new vendor categories: Social and Marketing, for the Facebook, Instagram, Google Business and mailing-list accounts that were never on the old spreadsheet and so had nowhere to go.
  • Add them with + ADD VENDOR on the Vendors tab. Existing entries are untouched.

0.31.1

  • Spacing fix: the add/edit vendor form now has a gap beneath it instead of butting up against the list.

0.31.0

  • Vendors is a list now, not a grid of cards. One row per vendor with vendor, phone, account number, login, password and website in aligned columns, so you can scan straight down a single column instead of hunting across boxes.
  • Address, fax and rep notes are tucked behind a caret on each row — click to open, so the list stays tight but nothing is lost.
  • Phone numbers are still tap-to-call and passwords still hide behind SHOW.

0.30.1

  • Fixes the portal rendering as unstyled text in 0.28.0–0.30.0. The vendor tab’s JavaScript was written into the middle of the stylesheet instead of the script block, so every style rule after that point stopped applying — the board, header and tabs all lost their formatting. The code is now where it belongs and the styling is back. No data was affected.

0.30.0

  • Fixed: completing an exchange sent the customer a vague second email. Marking one Shipped or Ready for Pickup completes the WooCommerce order, and Woo then sent its stock “your order is complete” notice on top of ours — which says nothing about whether the replacement is in the post or sitting on the counter. Woo’s version is now held back so only the exchange email goes out, and it always names which of the two it is.
  • The hold-back is stamped on the order and lasts five minutes, so a genuine order-complete email later on still sends normally. An order note records that it happened.
  • Ready for Pickup now asks before it emails, the same way Shipped does — it tells the customer to drive to Oswego, so it is worth one confirmation that the bag is actually on the shelf.
  • Marking one Ready for Pickup now shows a confirmation in the portal that the customer was told. Previously only Received and Shipped did, so pickups looked like nothing had happened.

0.29.0

  • New accounts get a password, not a link. Creating someone now generates a short readable password like KTM-8412, shows it to you on screen so you can read it out or text it, and emails it with their username and the portal address. No link to click, nothing to expire, nothing to lose to a spam folder.
  • Send reset does the same thing. It issues a fresh password and shows it to you immediately, so someone locked out at a press can be read their way back in.
  • The portal asks them to pick their own once they’re in. They can skip it — it just asks again at the next sign-in rather than blocking them.
  • Passwords avoid characters that are ambiguous out loud: no O or 0, no I or 1.
  • Each person gets a different one. A single shared default that is optional to change is the shared page password again, which is what all of this replaced.

0.28.0

  • New Vendors tab under Other. The old shared spreadsheet, imported and untangled — 88 vendors with phone, fax, account number, login, website, address and rep notes, grouped into categories and searchable by any field.
  • Passwords are hidden behind a SHOW button, encrypted at rest, and hide themselves again after 30 seconds so they aren’t left on screen at a shared machine. A COPY button puts one on the clipboard without displaying it.
  • Every reveal is logged — who looked at which vendor, and when.
  • Any portal user can look a vendor up; only portal admins can add, edit or delete. Editing another field never wipes a password you didn’t retype.
  • The import fixes the shifted columns from the old sheet, where credentials sat in the address field and account numbers in the fax field. Rows that were genuinely ambiguous are flagged in Notes rather than guessed at.

0.27.0

  • Portal User is now the everyday role you wanted. Schedule, stores, exchanges, scanners, quote and redirect — everything staff actually do — but no backups and no sight of anyone else’s account. Nothing to configure; it is what the role does now.
  • Backups are restricted to portal admins. The clock icon in the header is hidden for regular users, and more importantly the backup, restore and delete endpoints now require the capability — they were previously reachable by anyone at all, logged in or not. A restore silently replaces the entire board, so this was the sharpest edge in the plugin.
  • The nightly automatic backup is unaffected; it runs on a scheduled task, not through those endpoints.

0.26.0

  • The admin user list is now one line per person. It was a tall card each; it is a dense table now — username, name, email and old name all inline and editable, with the whole team visible at once instead of two people per screen.
  • Add people without leaving the portal. A single row at the top of the list takes a username, name, email, old name and user-or-admin, and sends the invite. No wp-admin.
  • Make admin, remove admin and remove access are icon buttons on each row. A coloured dot shows at a glance who is a portal user, a portal admin, or a WordPress admin.
  • A row you have edited turns yellow until it is saved, so nothing gets typed and abandoned.
  • You cannot change or remove your own access, and WordPress administrators are managed under Users — enforced on the server, not just hidden.

0.25.0

  • Fixed: the WordPress page password showed up before the portal login. /employees/ still carried the old shared page password, and WordPress checks that before the page renders at all — so staff got a password box, then a login screen. The portal page now ignores it. An admin notice points at the page so the setting can be cleared properly.
  • Fixed: a stale login form silently rejected a correct password. If the login page had been sitting open a long time its security token expired, and the form came back blank with no explanation — indistinguishable from a wrong password. It now says so and a refresh fixes it.
  • New Unlock button on Portal Users clears the 15 minute cooldown after too many failed login attempts, so nobody has to sit and wait it out.

0.24.0

  • Click your name in the header to open your account. Everyone sees their username and email, and a button that emails them a password reset link — no need to find an admin to get back in.
  • Username and email are read-only for regular portal users. Only an admin changes those.
  • Admins get the full list in the same panel. Edit anyone’s name, email and old name, and send them a password link, without leaving the portal. Renaming yourself refreshes the header so you can see it took.
  • The five account routes are capability-checked on the server, not just hidden in the panel.

0.23.0

  • Fixed: the portal header could show the wrong person’s name. The name comes from Old name when one is set, otherwise the display name — and neither could be corrected after the account was made. Both are now editable on the Portal Users screen, with a Shown as column so you can see exactly what the header will say.
  • WordPress administrators now appear on the Portal Users list. Administrators have always been able to open the portal, but they were invisible on this screen, so an admin account stamped with the wrong name had nowhere to be fixed. Their role is still managed under Users — this screen only sets what the portal calls them.
  • The portal page is now excluded from page caching. It carries the signed-in name, so a cached copy could show one person’s name to whoever opened it next.

0.22.0

  • Invite links now let people pick their own password on the portal. The email opens the portal login page with a “set your password” screen instead of sending them to the WordPress login. They set it, and they’re signed straight in — no second login screen. Links last 24 hours, and an expired one offers to send a fresh link.
  • The key from the email is moved out of the address bar into a short-lived cookie on arrival, so it can’t leak through browser history or a referrer on a shared shop computer. Clicking an invite while signed in as someone else signs that person out first.
  • New Portal Admin role. A portal admin can add, invite and remove portal logins without being a WordPress administrator — no access to plugins, settings or the rest of the site. Set it when creating a user, or use Make admin / Remove admin on the list.
  • Portal admins who aren’t WordPress administrators get their own Portal Users menu, since the BT Portal settings menu stays administrator-only.
  • Nobody can remove their own admin access or their own portal access by mistake.
  • Forgot-password emails for portal accounts now point at the portal too.

0.21.0

  • Real logins replace the shared page password. The portal now shows its own login screen. Each person gets a username, an email and their own password, created under BT Portal → Portal Users. Leave the password box blank there and WordPress emails them a link to set their own, so nothing readable is ever stored or sent.
  • The “Who are you?” dropdown is gone. The header shows whoever is signed in, with a Log out link beside it. Names can no longer be picked, borrowed or left set to the last person who used that computer.
  • Existing history is preserved. Each account carries an Old name matching the name already stored on that person’s jobs, day notes and completions, so new work keeps landing under the same name.
  • Five bad password attempts on the same account and device trigger a 15 minute cooldown; failures never reveal whether a username exists.
  • Removing someone’s access pulls the portal role but leaves their account and their record on past jobs intact.
  • The Redirect tool’s default “anyone who can open the portal” setting now means genuine portal access rather than anyone who reaches the page.

0.20.3

  • Fix: clearing the Loc # on a job put it straight back. Saving a job with the location box empty didn’t save it empty — it wrote a 1 instead. The board looked right until the card was opened again, at which point the 1 was read back into the field and the Loc chip reappeared on the card. It read like the schedule was adding a location on its own; the save was doing it.
  • A blank Loc # now stays blank, on the card and in the box, however many times the job is edited. Jobs with more than one line can have a location on some lines and not others.
  • Nothing already saved changes. A job that genuinely has 1 location still reads 1 — only the blanks stop being filled in for you.

0.20.2

  • The Printavo connection reads the credentials that were already saved. The move into the plugin was looking for them under the wrong name, found nothing, and quietly sent every click to a search page. It now finds the existing email and token.
  • The Printavo page shows which saved setting the credentials are coming from, so an empty connection says so instead of failing silently.
  • Quotes open at their usual address again.

0.20.1

  • Order number links actually resolve now. 0.20.0 asked Printavo for orders using the wrong search argument, so every lookup came back empty and fell through to a search page. Corrected.
  • Quotes open at the quote page and invoices at the invoice page, instead of everything being sent to /invoices/.

0.20.0

  • Order number links work again on finished jobs. Clicking an order number on a job card stopped working once that job was invoiced in Printavo — the lookup only ever searched quotes. It now checks quotes and invoices both.
  • A number that still can’t be found opens a Printavo search for it instead of stopping with an alert.
  • Failed lookups are only remembered for five minutes, so a job that gets invoiced mid-week fixes itself.
  • The Printavo connection now lives in BT Portal › Printavo, with a test box and a cache flush. The old standalone snippet can be turned off.

0.19.0

  • OMG Scanner gets a link too. Scan the pile, click Open in OMG, and the orders search opens with exactly those orders — no copying, no pasting. OMG reads the numbers off its own address the same way Chipply does.
  • Both scanners now work identically: scan, click through, select all, process.
  • The paste-ready box is still there under Settings and full list, for when copying the numbers is what’s wanted.
  • Long piles split into batches, same as Chipply, so no link gets truncated.

0.18.1

  • Chipply Scanner steps now say what the batch is actually for: send to ShipStation, message customers, and/or update status on all orders.

0.18.0

  • Both scanners now put the parts production actually touch — the readout, the counts and the buttons — inside one raised box, with everything else folded away under Settings and full list.
  • Nothing was removed: the scan gap, the beep, the search and the full list are all one click away, and they keep working while folded.

0.17.1

  • Shorter steps on both scanners — five on OMG, six on Chipply, one line each. The pickup-only warning moved to the bottom of the OMG list, where it reads as a rule rather than a step.

0.17.0

  • Both scanner tabs now have a numbered how-to down the side, so anyone can be handed a pile of slips and work it out without being shown first.
  • The two are different jobs, so the steps are different: OMG ends with copying the numbers and pasting them into OMG, Chipply ends with one click through to Order Manager. The OMG list leads with pickups only.
  • On a phone or a narrow window the steps move above the scanner instead of squeezing beside it.

0.16.0

  • Chipply Barcoder is hidden. Chipply now stamps a scannable barcode on its own order pages, so the tab had nothing left to do day to day. Nothing was deleted — it can be put back whenever it’s wanted.
  • Hiding it also takes about 900KB of PDF libraries out of every portal page load. Those were being fetched on every page, not just when the tab was open.

0.15.1

  • OMG Scanner now says up front that it’s for pickup orders only, since OMG can only bulk process pickups — a shipping order scanned there won’t go through with the batch.

0.15.0

  • New: Chipply Scanner, under Other. Scan a stack of slips, then click through to Order Manager with exactly those orders already filtered and ready to select — so labels and status changes can be done on the whole batch at once, instead of typing each order into the filter and clicking the name one at a time.
  • Long lists are split into batches, because an over-long link gets truncated and would quietly drop orders off the end. Each batch is its own link and nothing is lost between them.
  • Same scanning as the OMG tab: no Enter needed from the gun, typing waits for Enter, repeats flash red. A repeat is never sent to Chipply twice.
  • Deep link: /employees/chipply-scanner.

0.14.0

  • New: Chipply Barcoder, under Other. Drop a Chipply order export onto the page and every sheet comes back with a scannable Code 128 of its own order number stamped into the footer. Print it, or save the file.
  • The barcode goes in the strip the footer text already occupies, beside the page number — nothing on the sheet moves and no page grows taller.
  • It all runs in the browser: the file is never uploaded and never stored. A full day — 184 pages, 4MB — takes about three seconds, and the saved file is the same size as the one you dropped in.
  • Any page whose footer can’t be read is passed through untouched and listed by page number, rather than being stamped somewhere wrong.
  • Deep link: /employees/chipply-barcoder.

0.13.0

  • OMG Scanner: you can type into it now, as well as scan. The tab used to decide a code had ended purely by waiting for a pause, which suited the gun and quietly ate anything typed — each letter timed out on its own and was dropped for being too short. It now tells the two apart by speed: the gun’s characters land milliseconds apart and commit themselves instantly, so scanning a stack is unchanged, while anything typed at human speed stays on screen and waits for Enter.
  • A typed number is visible as you go, with Backspace to correct it and Escape to throw it away.
  • Paste a whole column of numbers onto the page — from a spreadsheet or anywhere else — and they all go in at once.

0.12.1

  • Fix: the last scan stayed on screen after Clear All. The big readout was only ever written when a code came in, so clearing the list — or deleting the last row — left that number sitting there in 72px type while every counter read zero. It now reads from the list itself, so it empties when the list does, and it shows the last code again after a refresh instead of the placeholder.

0.12.0

  • New: OMG Scanner, under Other. OMG packing slips carry a QR of the order number, but the gun sends the digits with no Enter after them — so working through a stack meant reaching for the keyboard between every single scan. The tab reads the end of each code from the gun’s own timing instead, so you scan straight down the pile and never touch the keyboard.
  • Numbers collect in a paste-ready box as you go, separated by a space, new line, comma or tab, with an option to end on a separator too. Copy the lot in one go, or download it as a CSV with timestamps.
  • Scanning the same order twice flashes red, beeps low and tags the row Repeat, so a double-scan is caught at the bench rather than in the numbers afterwards.
  • Capture only listens while the tab is open, so scans on the Schedule board never collect here. The list survives a refresh, and clearing it is the only way anything leaves.
  • Deep link: /employees/omg-scanner.

0.11.2

  • Fix: dragging a job card up a day column didn't stick. The board had the new order on screen but nothing that rendered it again knew about it, so the card jumped back — on the 15-second refresh, on a filter click, on any save. Three separate causes, all fixed.
  • Jobs came back from the server carrying their saved order and it was thrown away on the way in, so every render fell back to whatever order the array happened to be in.
  • The 15-second auto-refresh held off while a card was being dragged, but not while the new order was still being written. A refresh landing in that gap read the old order back and undid the move.
  • A drag now takes effect locally the moment it's dropped, so a render before the save lands keeps the new position. If the save actually fails it says so instead of silently reverting.
  • Completed jobs still sink to the bottom of the day; everything above them now sits in the order you put it in.
  • The card is no longer restyled in the same instant the drag starts, which is what made a drag occasionally refuse to begin at all.

0.11.1

  • Return Tracking is no longer its own column. The tracking box now sits under Ship in the Out column, and pickup rows don't get one — nothing is in the post.

0.11.0

  • New status: Ready for Pickup. A row only offers the ending that applies to it — a pickup exchange can't be marked Shipped, and a shipped one can't be marked Ready for Pickup. Whatever a row is already set to stays in its list, so nothing existing can vanish.
  • Moving an exchange in the portal now moves the WooCommerce order with it. Awaiting Items and Received hold it at Processing; Shipped and Ready for Pickup complete it. Cancelled, refunded, failed, unpaid and hidden orders are left alone.
  • Ready for Pickup sends the customer its own branded email — their replacement is finished and waiting in Oswego, with the address. Sends once, and never asks for tracking.

0.10.0

  • Two new columns, In and Out, sitting between New Size and Status. In reads Mailed or Drop off; Out reads Ship or Pickup. Every row carries both, so the two legs can be scanned down the table rather than hunted for.
  • Drop off and Pickup are coloured; Mailed and Ship stay grey, so the rows that change what you physically do are the ones that catch the eye.
  • Replaces the badges that sat in the Order cell in 0.9.0.

0.9.2 — Redirect works for everyone on the portal

  • Anyone who can open the portal can now use Redirect, same as every other tab. No WordPress account needed.
  • Redirect was the only tab that asked for a WordPress login, and its save/edit/delete endpoints were registered for signed-in users only — so staff without their own WordPress account couldn't use it whatever their role was.
  • If you ever want it held to a higher bar than the rest of the portal, BT Portal → Redirect access still offers the WordPress-account options.

0.9.1

  • Who can use the Redirect tool is now set in BT Portal → Redirect access — from any signed-in user up to administrators only. The default is unchanged (Contributor and up), so nobody's access changes until you change it.
  • The refusal message now says what to do about it, and tells someone who simply isn't signed in that that's the problem. It used to say only "You do not have permission to use this tool", which reads the same either way.
  • Signed-out visitors are never let in, whatever the setting.

0.9.0

  • Exchanges now show how each one travels. A Drop off badge means the customer is bringing the items in; a Pickup — do not ship badge means the finished exchange is collected at the shop and must not go in a mailer. Mail in and ship back is the default and is left unbadged, so only the exceptions catch the eye.
  • Read from the order, then from the Exchange Shipping line, then defaulted — everything placed before customers had the choice reads as mail in, ship back.

0.8.1

  • A combined item string keeps its blank positions, so an item with a colour but no size no longer slides the colour up into the Size column.

0.8.0

  • Orig Order # is its own column, with a badge reading OMG for a 9-digit number starting 1 and Chipply for a 7-digit number starting 8. Neither pattern, no badge — it is left blank rather than guessed.
  • The Product cell no longer repeats the order number and School/Team when there are no item rows. Both have their own columns; they were being printed a second time by the raw-meta fallback.
  • Exchange details are now read from labelled meta on the Exchange Shipping line as well as from order meta and the old customer note, and the three are merged rather than raced. Item fields are matched by name (Item 1 Product, Item 1 Size, Item 1 Color, Item 1 Qty, Item 1 New Size), or as one combined string, so Size/Color/Qty/New Size fill in as soon as the form writes them — no plugin release needed to match.

0.7.4 — fixes empty tables on /employees/<tab> links

  • Nothing was ever lost. Tab links stopped WordPress redirecting boomerts.com to www.boomerts.com, so the portal sat on the bare host while the API lived on www — a different origin, so every call failed and the tables came up blank.
  • Host and https corrections are allowed through again; only redirects that would strip the tab off the path are blocked.
  • A failed load now says so and says nothing has been lost, instead of showing an empty table.

0.7.3

  • Received email now reads "usually take up to 7–10 days" — a ceiling, not a promise.

0.7.2

  • The exchange emails are properly Boomer T's now: the logo on a navy header with the pink rule under it, navy section bar, and pink for the new size and the tracking callout. They were using the flat blue off the printed slip with no logo at all.
  • Logo URL, navy and pink are set in BT Portal → Customer email branding, so the brand can move without a plugin release.

0.7.1

  • Marking an exchange Shipped with no tracking number now stops and asks: No Tracking Number Entered. Are you sure you want to mark this order as shipped and notify the customer?
  • Saying no saves nothing and puts the dropdown back where it was. A row that already has a tracking number is never questioned.

0.7.0

  • Marking Received emails the customer — their package arrived, we're on it, we'll ship as soon as we can.
  • Marking Shipped emails them the tracking number, with what went in and what's going out.
  • Both are Boomer T's branded and match the printed slip they already have. Replies come back to the shop.
  • Set Shipped before you have a tracking number and they still get the heads-up; paste the number in afterwards and they get exactly one follow-up with it. Correcting a number later does not re-mail anyone.
  • Nothing sends twice, whatever order the dropdown gets clicked in, and nothing sends on hidden, cancelled, refunded, failed or unpaid orders.
  • Every send is written onto the WooCommerce order, and the portal tells you on screen that the customer was mailed.

0.6.7

  • Exchanges checks for new orders once a minute while that tab is open. Switch away and the timer is cleared, so no other part of the portal pays for it.
  • A new one arriving says so; nothing else on screen moves.
  • It holds off while you're typing in a Tracking or Notes box, so a refresh can never wipe a half-entered number, and it skips entirely while the window is in the background — coming back catches up straight away instead of waiting out the minute.
  • Nothing repaints unless something actually changed, so the table doesn't flicker once a minute for no reason.

0.6.6

  • School / Team moved inside the item block, so it now reads School / Team → Product → Size → Color → Qty → New Size as one group: everything about what is being exchanged, ruled off from who the customer is.

0.6.5

  • Product is no longer the widest thing on the screen. It had no width set, so it was soaking up all the leftover space and pushing Size, Color, Qty and New Size across the table away from it.
  • Those five now sit together as one tinted, ruled-off block, with a clear break before Status.
  • Customer takes the leftover width instead — the address stops wrapping onto three lines.

0.6.4

  • The exchange itself is now real columns: Product, Size, Color, Qty, New Size — the same shape as the form and the printed slip.
  • A request with more than one item stacks its values in each of the five columns in the same order, so line two of Product lines up with line two of Size, Color, Qty and New Size.
  • Qty is called out when it is more than one.
  • An order with nothing structured recorded says so in Product and dashes the rest, rather than faking columns out of a sentence.

0.6.3

  • Exchanges now read the request straight off the order (_bt_exchange_items, _bt_original_order, _bt_school_team) instead of reading the note. Exact fields, no guessing at wording.
  • School / Team fills from _bt_school_team as soon as the form sends it.
  • Quantity shows when a customer is exchanging more than one of the same thing — it was being dropped.
  • Note parsing stays as a fallback and now understands both wordings, so older orders still display.

0.6.2

  • Standing notice on the Quote tab: this page's address is the employee portal, customers can't open it, and the link won't carry the quote — use Copy Quote Link, which makes a boomerts.com/quote link.
  • Copying any portal URL out of the page now pops a warning with the public quoter link. Copying ordinary text, or a real /quote/ link, stays silent.
  • Copy Quote Link confirms what staff actually need to know — that the link works for customers.
  • Note: nothing on a web page can see a copy made from the browser's address bar. The notice on the tab is what covers that.

0.6.1

  • Exchanges is now Order, Customer, School / Team, Exchanging, For, Status, Return Tracking, Notes, Hide.
  • What came in and what goes out are their own columns, rendered in lockstep so a multi-item request stays lined up across both.
  • School / Team column, read from the request note, from order meta, or from meta on the shipping line — whichever the form ends up using. It will fill in on its own once the field is added to the form; no plugin release needed to match.
  • The customer's original order number moved up into the Order cell, next to the Woo order it belongs with.

0.6.0

  • Every tab has its own link. /employees/exchanges, /employees/online-stores, /employees/quote, /employees/redirect, /employees/contacts. Schedule stays on plain /employees/.
  • The URL follows as you click, so a refresh keeps you where you were and you can send someone straight to a tab.
  • Back and Forward walk through the tabs instead of leaving the portal.
  • The route is built from whichever page holds the shortcode, not a hardcoded "employees" — renaming or moving the portal page keeps working.
  • If permalinks are plain, it falls back to ?tab=exchanges rather than inventing a path that would 404.
  • After updating, open the portal once. That registers the page and the links go live on the next load. If a deep link 404s, go to Settings → Permalinks and hit Save once.

0.5.5

  • Plugin flags no longer show up as exchange details. is_vat_exempt, tefw_exempt and anything else that is a bare yes/no or a system field are filtered out — they tell nobody processing an exchange anything.
  • Real details still come through, and field names now read as words (Exchange Reason, not exchange_reason).
  • If something else creeps in later, it can be added to the btp_exchange_meta_blocklist filter without a release.

0.5.4

  • The exchange request is no longer one run-on paragraph. It reads as fields: original order number on its own line, the item ordered with size and colour as chips, and an arrow to what they want instead. Multi-item requests come through as separate blocks.
  • If the wording ever changes and the parse fails, the note is still shown in full — nothing gets swallowed.
  • Details attached to the Exchange Shipping line itself, and custom fields on the order, are now shown too. They were being thrown away, which is why some orders looked empty.
  • An order with nothing recorded anywhere now says so plainly and links straight into Woo, instead of showing a blank cell.
  • Dropped the "Shipping only" line — it was on every single row and said nothing.

0.5.3

  • Orders that haven't been paid for no longer read as live exchanges. They show Woo's own wording — Pending payment, On hold — as a pill instead of a status dropdown, sit dimmed, and have their own Unpaid filter.
  • They are out of the Awaiting Items count, so that number is now only exchanges someone is actually waiting on a box for.
  • Read from Woo on every load: the moment payment lands, the row rejoins the queue on its own with nothing to click.

0.5.2

  • Fix: the portal URL got stuck on quote parameters. Touching the Quote tab rewrote the address bar to /employees/?qty=4&g=supplied&loc=2, and it stayed there through refreshes and bookmarks. The quote tool syncs the URL on /quote/ by design; it is now told not to when it is one tab of the portal.
  • Copy Quote Link in the Quote tab now hands you a /quote/ link. It was building the link off whatever page it was on, so a quote link copied from here sent the customer to the employee portal.
  • Parameters already stuck on the URL are cleared once, on load.
  • Needs BT Quote 0.4.1 or newer — update that one too.

0.5.1

  • The seven test orders (4980, 4457, 4456, 4455, 4454, 4453, 4452) are hidden on first load after this update.
  • Hide / Restore on every row — nothing is deleted, hidden rows move to their own filter and can be brought back. The next test order doesn't need a plugin release.
  • Cancelled, refunded and failed orders no longer sit in the pending pile. They get their own filter and a Cancelled pill instead of a status dropdown, so nobody can march a dead order through to Shipped. Read from Woo on every load — reinstate the order in wp-admin and it rejoins the queue on its own.

0.5.0

  • Tab bar is now Schedule, Online Stores, Quote, Redirect and an Other dropdown. Contacts moved into Other; the pill shows which section you're in and the menu closes on Esc, on selection, or on a click anywhere else.
  • New: Exchanges. Every order containing the Exchange Shipping product, in one list — order number and link into wp-admin, customer and return address, what they're exchanging for (including whatever the form attached to the line), and the customer's note.
  • Each exchange tracks Awaiting Items → Received → Shipped, plus a return tracking number and a notes field. Saves as you change it, records who changed it, and writes a note onto the WooCommerce order so the history lives with the order too.
  • Filter pills across the top with live counts, so "what's still waiting to come back" is one click.
  • Woo owns the order; the portal only stores where the exchange physically is. Nothing is copied out of Woo, so an order edited in wp-admin is never stale here.
  • The Exchange Shipping product ID is set in BT Portal → Exchanges (default 4441), so the product can be rebuilt in Woo without a plugin release.
  • Exchange routes require the portal's wp_rest nonce — like the order-completion endpoint, and unlike the open job/store routes, since they read customer addresses and write order notes.
  • Security fix: the Contacts tab rendered website form submissions as raw HTML. Anything a stranger typed into the contact form — including a script tag — ran in the browser of whichever employee opened the tab. All contact fields are now escaped.

0.4.0

  • Every BT plugin now shows the same Updates section in the same place — last on the page, same heading, same button, same wording. Shared file, so they cannot drift apart again.
  • Added a Status heading above the portal stats table.

0.3.2

  • Art paths now work from a Mac. The board still stores one canonical UNC path (what the btart:// helper on the production PCs opens), but the field accepts whatever anyone pastes and converts it: Finder Copy as Pathname, a dragged file (file:// with %20 spaces), Connect to Server smb:// or afp:// URLs, Explorer's quoted copy-as-path, forward-slash UNC, and mapped drive letters.
  • Duplicate mounts are handled — a share that comes back as BTServer-1 or BTServer 2 resolves to the same server path instead of a dead link.
  • Live preview under the Art field shows exactly what the production PC will open, as you type. Green when it resolves cleanly, amber when it's a guess or a mapped drive, red when it's a folder on your own machine that nobody else can reach.
  • ART button on the card works on a Mac too — Macs get an smb:// link into Finder, PCs keep the btart:// helper.
  • Server name is one editable line (BT_ART_HOST) instead of being buried in a regex; BT_ART_HOST_BY_SHARE handles any share that lives on a different box.
  • Existing saved paths are already canonical and pass through untouched.

0.3.1

  • FIX: clicking a job card did nothing. BT Quote's submit modal uses id="btModalOverlay" — the same id as the portal's job modal. Since 0.2.5 renders BT Quote's markup inside the Quote tab, two elements shared that id and BT Quote's came first in the document, so btOpenModal() opened its overlay — which lives inside the hidden Quote tab. The click always fired; the modal opened where it couldn't be seen.
  • Portal's job modal is now btpJobModalOverlay, and the four class names both plugins shared (bt-modal-overlay, bt-modal-close, bt-modal-body, bt-modal-footer) are btp- prefixed. No ids and no classes overlap between the two plugins now.
  • Modal z-index restored to the portal's 999999 (it had been silently inheriting BT Quote's 99999).

0.3.0

  • Transfers job cards now have a COMPLETE ORDER button. One click marks the matching WooCommerce order Completed, which fires Woo's own Completed-order email to the customer — no separate step in wp-admin.
  • Confirms first: the button looks the order up and shows order number, customer, email, total, item count and current status before anything is sent. Nothing goes out on a mis-click.
  • Order number is resolved server-side from the card itself, never passed in from the browser. Handles 5088, #5088 and prefixed/sequential numbers.
  • Won't touch cancelled, refunded or failed orders, and never re-fires the email on an order that is already Completed.
  • The card records what happened (woo_order_id, woo_completed_at, woo_completed_by), flips to Complete/Notify Customer, and the button becomes a static ORDER DONE tick so it can't be double-sent.
  • This is the one portal endpoint that is not open — it requires the portal's wp_rest nonce, since it mutates orders and emails customers.

0.2.6

  • FIX header: 0.2.5 changed the reset to *:not(.bt-tool):not(.bt-tool *), which raised its specificity to 1,2,0 and made it outrank the header rules, crushing the top bar. Now wrapped in :where(), which contributes zero specificity — reset is back to 1,0,0 and still skips the quote tool.
  • FIX quote tool: BT Quote enqueues its CSS and JS from inside its own shortcode; this template never printed them, so the tool rendered as bare HTML with no styling and no JS. The portal now emits both files directly in the tab, in order (CSS, markup, config, JS), and dequeues the copies BT Quote queued so nothing loads twice.
  • Still the same files from bt-quote/assets — one tool, one pricing engine, no portal copy.

0.2.5

  • The Quote tab is now the exact same tool as the public /quote/ page — BT Quote's [bt_quick_quote], one codebase, no portal copy to drift.
  • Two reasons it came through bare before: BT Quote's stylesheet was enqueued mid-content so it landed late or not at all, and the portal reset (#bt-schedule-app *, specificity 1,0,0) outranked every class rule in it. Now the stylesheet is enqueued up front on the portal page, and the reset skips the .bt-tool subtree entirely.
  • No spacing rules duplicated into the portal — BT Quote styles its own tool, so the two stay identical automatically.

0.2.4

  • Quote tab prices again. Same card, same layout — only the values it sends changed to match BT Quote 0.3.1: garment IDs instead of generic names, "embroidery" instead of "emb", embType instead of emb_type, retail instead of garment_cost, and it reads perShirt instead of each.
  • The garment dropdown is now generated from BT Quote's own pricing tables at render time, so it can never drift from the engine again.
  • Max Colors removed — BT Quote prices full colour by location, so the dropdown never changed the number.
  • Locations capped at 3 (the engine's limit). Embroidery over the by-quote minimum shows "By Quote" instead of an error.

0.2.3

  • Quote tab restored to exactly what the snippet port shipped. 0.2.1 (swapping in BT Quote's shortcode) and 0.2.2 (CSS to compensate for it) are both reverted. The portal frontend is byte-identical to v0.2.0 again — the port stays invisible to employees.

0.2.2

  • Fix: Quote tab layout — the portal's universal CSS reset (#bt-schedule-app *) outranked BT Quote's stylesheet and flattened every margin, padding and gap in the quote tool, collapsing the cards into a run-together mess. The tool's spacing is now re-stated at matching specificity so the reset can't win.

0.2.1

  • FIX: Quote tab showed "Pricing error" and a plain form. The portal was carrying its own copy of the quote UI from the July 24 port, built against BT Quote v0.1.0. BT Quote is now v0.3.1 and its /price endpoint expects garment IDs (g5000, bc3001, supplied, custom) instead of generic labels (tshirt, hoodie), so every request came back 400 invalid_garment.
  • The Quote tab now renders BT Quote's own [bt_quick_quote] shortcode. One quote UI, maintained in one place, no drift.
  • Removed 189 lines of duplicated quote code from the portal.

  • Redirect module ported in from BT-Sched-5-Redirect — the /stores/ redirect portal and [bt_redirect_tab] now ship with the plugin. Deactivate the old snippet after updating.
  • Redirect tab: copy button on each URL Path row copies the full https link to the clipboard.
  • All option names, post meta keys, AJAX actions and the shortcode tag are unchanged, so existing redirect pages and click counts carry over untouched.
